newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil, fuel oil up on demand.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil, fuel oil up on demand.

text.p: Singapore gas oil and fuel oil swaps rose late afternoon on Wednesday as the market was bought up by some players on expectations of fresh demand from regional buyers, traders said.
The hike on gas oil, which has gained about 60 cents per barrel from Tuesday, was mainly attributed to firmer prices in the West and the belief that the market here has bottomed.
Fuel oil rose by $1.25 per tonne from Tuesday amid improved bunker demand and tight supplies, traders said.
August gas oil was last quoted at $23.45/$23.60, up from Monday's $22.95/$23.05. September was quoted at $24.00/$24.10, up from Tuesday's at $23.75/$23.85, brokers said.
September traded earlier in the day at $24.05, $24.12 and $24.15 per barrel, they said.
The focus on the front month August has narowed the August/September time spread which traded earlier in the day at minus 60 cents, compared to Tuesday's minus 75 cents trade, brokers said.
September/October traded at minus 55 cents and minus 50 cents.
Traders said the firmer August prices were due to expectations of fresh but scattered demand from local traders as seen in the physical market this week.
On Tuesday, a 150,000-barrel cargo traded at $22.90 per barrel free-on-board Singapore basis for August 22-29 lifting, up 40 cents from Monday's traded level.

The jet fuel/gas oil spread or regrade rose sharply even though outright gas oil swaps values have also jumped as buyers entered the market in anticipation of fresh jet fuel demand as players stock up for the winter.
August regrade was last quoted at 1.20/1.50 cents compared to Tuesday's 50/70 cents, brokers said. August regrade traded at $1.20 per barrel.
Fuel oil extended its early week rally on strong bunker demand and tight supplies.
August and September swaps were last quoted at $103.75/$104.50 per tonne, from Tuesday's $102.50/$103.00, brokers said.
Both months traded earlier in the day at $103.75 and $104.00 per tonne, they said.
